body: People make visual objects, sounds, movements and stories that can express experiences and carry knowledge. A song can accompany work or a celebration. Cloth can protect a body and reflect skills or meanings learned among its makers. Games can be recreational and also teach shared rules or skills.

Knowledge about making things and organizing daily life can pass between people through language, imitation, demonstration and participation. Habits vary between households and communities. A museum record of a musical instrument and a photograph of weaving document different practices. Each leaves out sound, movement and the wider circumstances of use.

limitations: Cultural meanings may differ among participants and change over time. Some practices and records carry restrictions set by communities, and an archive needs their context and permissions.
purpose: Introduce artistic expression and everyday cultural practice without assuming universal meanings.

revision_history.change: Connected everyday practices and transmission of know-how while clarifying the limits of individual records
